agent_notes: אָקוּט is read as 'I loathed' (Rashi cites Job 10:1; Ibn Ezra the same). Radak and Metzudat Zion derive it from קטטה 'quarrel'; I mention this but do not follow it. בְּדוֹר has no 'this/that' in the Hebrew; KJV's 'this generation' is an addition.

אִם is the oath formula with the curse suppressed ('if they enter...' = 'they shall surely not enter'); Radak and Metzudat David say so, citing Ps 89:36 ('if I lie to David'). The literal layer keeps the broken 'if' and the dramatic layer gives the sense.

agent_notes: נִבְרְכָה is glossed 'let us kneel' (from ברך 'knee'), not 'bless' (same consonants, different root). Rashi and Ibn Ezra both read it as kneeling. The three verbs (bow, bend, kneel) are three postures; Radak's definitions of each are cited.

Addressed the reviewer request: the commentary no longer calls the 'you' a different speaker's voice. It says the speaker turns from 'we' to 'you' at 'today', and that God's own first-person voice enters only at v9 ('they tested me'). The five English versions split on the last clause: KJV, YLT and Webster leave it as an open 'if' clause, ASV and BBE make it a wish ('oh that…'). The literal layer keeps the open 'if'; the dramatic layer lets the clause hang unfinished, since the Hebrew gives no apodosis.
